primary_work.title: Models with a Cause: Causal Discovery with Language Models on Temporally Ordered Text Data

decision: NARROWED BEYOND TOKEN-LEVEL CAUSAL DISCOVERY AND LANGUAGE-DYNAMICS PRETRAINING — NOT ADOPTED
prior_art_boundary: temporal ordering in text as causal orientation information is prior art
testing language models for token-level conditional independence and Markov exchangeability is prior art
mixtures of Markov chains and synthetic token interventions are established controlled tests for language dynamics
qualitative causal probability rankings need not imply exact density recovery
successful token-level causal discovery or language-dynamics pretraining does not by itself identify environment grounding, raw-utterance equivalence, latent intervention targets, or denotation
counterexample: Two models related by joint recoding of vocabulary symbols, utterance classes, latent target blocks, denotation, language encoder, and policy/decoder preserve the full token causal law, temporal conditional independencies, Markov exchangeability, intervention rankings, language loss, next-state prediction, action accuracy, task success, and language-shuffle effects while assigning different external meanings. Even without vocabulary recoding, two utterances with identical token-context and environment behavior can be modeled as synonyms or as distinct observationally aliased meanings. Therefore language dynamics and task control identify at most a predictive/control code unless an independently fixed cross-system anchor removes the residual automorphism.
official_code_status: paper-specific official code verified and exact commit pinned; synthetic generators, intervention generation, four architecture families, conditional-independence, exchangeability, intervention, hyperparameter-search, training, and experiment scripts are present; README documents five-seed averaging, but immutable dataset/model/resource/checksum manifests and a containerized R0 contract are not established
